stem: A nursing instructor explains that the vertebral column of a newborn shows only ONE type of curvature at birth. Which curvature classification does this represent, and why?
options: Secondary curvature, because it develops after weight-bearing begins
Primary curvature, because it is retained from the concave fetal posture
Compensatory curvature, because it balances the cervical curve
Pathological curvature, because the spine has not yet ossified

stem: At approximately what age does the secondary cervical curvature become established, and what functional milestone drives its development?
options: 12–15 months, when the infant begins to walk
3 months, when the infant begins to hold up the head
6 months, when the infant begins to sit unsupported
9 months, when the infant begins to crawl

stem: The secondary lumbar curvature develops in response to which milestone, and at approximately what age range?
Which pair of curvatures are classified as PRIMARY curvatures of the adult vertebral column, retained unchanged from fetal life?
A student mixes up curvature terminology. Which statement correctly distinguishes primary from secondary curvatures?
options: Primary curvatures are concave anteriorly (kyphotic); secondary curvatures are concave posteriorly (lordotic)
Primary curvatures appear only after birth; secondary curvatures are present in utero
Primary curvatures are lordotic; secondary curvatures are kyphotic
Primary and secondary curvatures both appear simultaneously at 3 months

stem: Which structure connects the laminae of adjacent vertebrae and is composed predominantly of elastic tissue, giving it a characteristic yellow appearance?
A ligament runs the entire length of the vertebral column along the anterior surface of the vertebral bodies, limiting excessive extension of the spine. This is the:
Which ligament lies INSIDE the vertebral canal, runs the whole length of the column along the posterior surface of the vertebral bodies, and helps limit hyperflexion?
The ligamentum nuchae is best described as a specialized extension of which structure, confined to which vertebral region?
options: The anterior longitudinal ligament; lumbar region

stem: Which ligament specifically holds the dens (odontoid process) of the axis in correct apposition against the anterior arch of the atlas, preventing posterior displacement into the spinal cord?
The supraspinous ligament connects the tips of the spinous processes and extends between which two landmarks?
options: From the atlas to the axis
From the occiput to the sacrum
From C7 to the coccyx only
From the manubrium to the xiphoid process

stem: An intervertebral disc herniates, and the nucleus pulposus bulges posterolaterally through a tear in the surrounding structure. This surrounding structure is the:
options: Articular cartilage of the facet joint

stem: Which best describes the composition of the nucleus pulposus of an intervertebral disc?
options: Dense fibrocartilage arranged in concentric rings
Gelatinous, semi-fluid material that absorbs compressive shock
Hyaline cartilage covering the vertebral end-plate

stem: Comparing disc thickness along the vertebral column, which statement is correct?
options: Discs are thickest in the cervical region and thinnest in the lumbar region
Discs are of uniform thickness throughout the column
Discs are thinnest in the cervical region and progressively thicker toward the lumbar region
Discs are thickest in the thoracic region only

stem: An intervertebral foramen is formed between which two structures of adjacent vertebrae?
options: The transverse processes of adjacent vertebrae
The spinous processes of adjacent vertebrae

stem: Structures that pass through the intervertebral foramina include all of the following EXCEPT:
Movement between adjacent vertebrae is described as very limited primarily because of which two factors?
options: Interlocking bony processes and supporting ligaments
The presence of the spinal cord and nerve roots

stem: Which movement of the vertebral column occurs at the LEAST range compared to flexion, extension, lateral flexion, and rotation?
options: Rotation is greatest, not least — flexion/extension have the largest range
There is no comparative restriction between movements

stem: A vertebra has a foramen within each transverse process through which the vertebral artery ascends to supply the brain. This feature is diagnostic of which vertebral region?
Why are cervical vertebrae the smallest in the vertebral column?
options: They bear the greatest compressive load of the entire trunk
They only need to support the weight of the head
They articulate with the ribs and must remain slender
They are fused and therefore reduced in individual size

stem: Which TWO cervical vertebrae are described as atypical, differing structurally from C3–C6?
The atlas (C1) is structurally unique in that it lacks which TWO features found in typical vertebrae?
options: Transverse processes and a vertebral foramen
A body and a spinous process

stem: The superior articular processes of the atlas articulate directly with which structure to permit nodding (flexion/extension) of the head?
options: The occipital condyles of the skull

stem: The dens (odontoid process) is a bony projection arising from the body of which vertebra, and it serves as a pivot for rotation of which structure?
options: The axis (C2); the atlas rotates around it
The atlas (C1); the axis rotates around it
C7; the atlas rotates around it
The axis (C2); the occipital bone rotates around it

stem: C7 is clinically termed the vertebra prominens because of which distinguishing feature?
options: It has bifid superior articular facets
It has a long, easily palpable spinous process that is not bifid
It has a foramen transversarium that admits the vertebral artery in unusually large volume
It fuses with the first thoracic vertebra in most adults

stem: Which feature distinguishes thoracic vertebrae from cervical vertebrae and correlates directly with their articulation with the ribs?
options: Presence of costal facets on the vertebral bodies and transverse processes

stem: Why are thoracic vertebral bodies and transverse processes generally larger than those of cervical vertebrae?
options: They must accommodate the spinal cord's cervical enlargement
They support more body weight and bear facets for rib articulation
They lack intervertebral discs and require greater surface area

stem: Which vertebrae are the LARGEST in the vertebral column, reflecting their role in supporting the weight of the entire upper body?
Lumbar vertebrae are characterized by substantial spinous processes that serve which primary functional purpose?
options: Attachment for the muscles of the lower back

stem: The sacrum is formed by the fusion of how many rudimentary vertebrae, and what overall shape does it take?
options: Four vertebrae; a small oval bone
Five vertebrae; a triangular, wedge-shaped bone
Three vertebrae; a curved crescent bone

stem: The base (superior surface) of the sacrum articulates with which vertebra above it?
The bony ridge on the anterior edge of the sacral base that protrudes into the pelvic cavity, used as an obstetric landmark, is called the:
On each lateral aspect of the sacrum, a joint is formed with the ilium of the pelvis. This is the:
The anterior and posterior sacral foramina exist along the sacrum primarily to transmit which structures?
The coccyx is formed by the fusion of how many rudimentary terminal vertebrae?
The coccyx articulates superiorly with which bony landmark?
A vertebral arch has how many articular surfaces that can be palpated through the skin along the length of the spine, and how do they distribute above and below?
options: Three total; one above, two below
Four total; two articulate with the vertebra above, two with the one below
Two total; one above, one below
Six total; three above, three below

stem: The thoracic cage is anatomically composed of the sternum, how many pairs of ribs, and how many thoracic vertebrae?
options: 10 pairs of ribs and 10 thoracic vertebrae
12 pairs of ribs and 12 thoracic vertebrae
11 pairs of ribs and 12 thoracic vertebrae
12 pairs of ribs and 11 thoracic vertebrae

stem: The sternum is composed of three parts. Which sequence correctly lists them from superior to inferior?
The manubrium of the sternum forms joints with the clavicles and provides attachment for which pairs of ribs?
options: The first two pairs of ribs
Only the first pair of ribs

stem: A palpable depression felt under the skin at the superior border of the manubrium, between the two sternoclavicular joints, is the:
The manubriosternal joint, palpable as a bony ridge where the manubrium meets the body of the sternum, is clinically referred to as the:
The sternal angle serves as a clinical landmark for locating which structure?
options: The 5th intercostal space at the midclavicular line
The costal cartilage of the 2nd rib

stem: The xiphoid process, the inferior tip of the sternum, gives attachment to which structures?
options: The diaphragm and the muscles of the anterior abdominal wall via the linea alba
The costal cartilages of ribs 1 and 2 only

stem: The 'white line' referred to in relation to the xiphoid process attachment of abdominal wall muscles is properly named the:
Ribs 1–7 connect directly to the sternum via their own costal cartilages and are classified as:
Ribs 8–10 do not attach directly to the sternum; instead, their costal cartilages fuse with the cartilage of the rib above. These are classified as:
Ribs 11 and 12 have free anterior tips that do not join the sternum at all. These are termed:
A typical rib forms up to three joints with the vertebral column. Which of the following pairings is CORRECT?
options: The tubercle articulates with facets on two vertebral bodies; the head articulates with the transverse process
The head articulates with facets on the bodies of two adjacent vertebrae; the tubercle articulates with the transverse process of the lower vertebra
The neck articulates with the lamina; the head articulates with the spinous process
The shaft articulates with the pedicle; the tubercle articulates with the body

stem: How many of the twelve ribs form a joint between their tubercle and the transverse process of the corresponding vertebra?
The deeply grooved inferior surface of a typical rib, which provides a channel for the intercostal nerve and blood vessels, is called the:
Which rib is firmly fixed to the sternum and to the first thoracic vertebra, remaining essentially immobile during quiet breathing while acting as the fixed point around which the ribcage moves?
During inspiration, contraction of the intercostal muscles pulls the entire ribcage as a unit toward which fixed structure?
The ribcage is described as a flexible structure that changes shape and size during breathing largely due to which two factors?
options: The number of muscle attachments and vertebral rotation
The arrangement of the ribs and the quantity of cartilage present
The density of the sternal bone and diaphragmatic tension
Fusion of costal cartilages and reduced rib mobility

stem: Intercostal muscles occupy the spaces between adjacent ribs and function primarily to:
options: Anchor the spinal cord within the vertebral canal

stem: CASE SCENARIO: A 68-year-old man presents with a stooped upper back posture that has progressively worsened over years, consistent with an exaggerated curvature. Given that this curvature is primary and concave anteriorly, which region is most affected?

CASE SCENARIO (continued): The nurse explains to the man's family that, unlike the thoracic curvature, the cervical and lumbar curvatures are classified differently in developmental terms because they:
options: Are present from birth and never change
Develop secondarily, after birth, in response to motor milestones
Are absent in the normal adult spine

stem: CASE SCENARIO: A radiographer notes a vertebra with a triangular vertebral foramen, a bifid spinous process, and a foramen within each transverse process. Which vertebral level is being described?

CASE SCENARIO (continued): The radiographer then identifies a separate vertebra lacking a body and spinous process altogether, with only anterior and posterior arches and lateral masses. This must be the:

CASE SCENARIO: A patient sustains trauma resulting in a fracture of the dens with disruption of the ligament holding it against the atlas. Which structure has most likely failed, placing the spinal cord at risk?

CASE SCENARIO: On MRI, a patient's L4–L5 intervertebral disc shows a posterior tear of the outer fibrocartilaginous ring with extrusion of the inner gelatinous core. This describes rupture of the annulus fibrosus with herniation of the:
CASE SCENARIO (continued): The patient's disc pathology is occurring at the lumbar level. The nurse recalls that lumbar discs are structurally different from cervical discs in that they are:
options: The same thickness as cervical discs
Absent, since lumbar vertebrae articulate directly bone-to-bone

stem: CASE SCENARIO: A trauma patient has a fractured rib with associated numbness along the corresponding intercostal space. The nurse recognizes that the intercostal nerve most likely coursed through which anatomical feature of the rib?
options: The costal groove on the inferior rib surface
The superior border of the rib

stem: CASE SCENARIO (continued): Imaging shows the fractured rib is the 11th rib, with a free anterior tip not attached to the sternum. The nurse correctly classifies this as a:
CASE SCENARIO: A clinician palpates a bony prominence at the level where the manubrium meets the sternal body to auscultate the second intercostal space. This palpable landmark is the:

CASE SCENARIO: During a difficult vaginal delivery, the obstetric team assesses pelvic capacity by palpating a bony prominence on the anterior sacral base that can narrow the pelvic inlet if excessively prominent. This landmark is the:
CASE SCENARIO: A newborn is examined and found to be curled with the head and knees almost touching. The nurse explains this fetal posture reflects which curvature pattern of the spine?
options: Only the primary (kyphotic) curvature, since secondary curvatures have not yet developed
An abnormal scoliotic curvature requiring referral

stem: Which of the following is an atypical vertebra that DOES bear a spinous process and body, distinguishing it from the truly atypical atlas?
options: Both atlas and axis are equally atypical with no body
Neither the atlas nor axis has a body

stem: Which statement about the vertebral artery's course is correct?
options: It passes through foramina in the transverse processes of thoracic vertebrae only
It passes upward through foramina in the transverse processes of cervical vertebrae to reach the brain
It passes through the vertebral foramen alongside the spinal cord
It passes through the intervertebral foramina of lumbar vertebrae

stem: Which of the following best differentiates the anterior longitudinal ligament from the posterior longitudinal ligament in terms of location relative to the vertebral bodies?
options: Both lie inside the vertebral canal
The anterior ligament lies in front of the vertebral bodies; the posterior ligament lies inside the vertebral canal, behind the bodies
The anterior ligament lies inside the vertebral canal; the posterior ligament lies in front of the bodies
Both lie lateral to the vertebral bodies

stem: The vertebral column exhibits ___________ primary curvature(s) and ___________ secondary curvature(s) when viewed from the side in the adult.
The secondary cervical curvature develops by about ___________ months of age, while the secondary lumbar curvature develops between ___________ and ___________ months of age.
The intervertebral disc consists of an outer ring of fibrocartilage called the ___________ and a central gelatinous core called the ___________.
An intervertebral foramen is formed between the ___________ of every pair of adjacent vertebrae.
The ligament that holds the dens of the axis in correct position relative to the atlas is the ___________ ligament.
The ___________ ligament runs the whole length of the vertebral column in front of the vertebral bodies, whereas the ___________ ligament lies inside the vertebral canal.
The sacrum consists of ___________ rudimentary vertebrae fused to form a single triangular bone, while the coccyx consists of ___________ fused terminal vertebrae.
The upper part of the sacrum, called the ___________, articulates with the 5th lumbar vertebra, and its anterior edge protrudes into the pelvic cavity as the ___________.
The thoracic cage is made up of the sternum anteriorly, ___________ pairs of ribs, and the ___________ thoracic vertebrae posteriorly.
The three parts of the sternum, listed from superior to inferior, are the ___________, the ___________, and the ___________.
The palpable notch felt under the skin at the superior border of the manubrium is called the ___________ notch.
The bony ridge palpable where the manubrium meets the body of the sternum, marking the level of the 2nd costal cartilage, is called the ___________.

Ribs 1 through 7 are classified as ___________ ribs because their costal cartilages attach directly to the sternum, while ribs 11 and 12 are classified as ___________ ribs because their anterior tips are free.

A typical rib forms joints with the vertebral column at the ___________, which articulates with facets on the bodies of two adjacent vertebrae, and the ___________, which articulates with the transverse process.
The deeply grooved inferior surface of a rib, providing a channel for the intercostal nerve and vessels, is called the ___________ ___________.
During inspiration, the intercostal muscles pull the entire ribcage upward as a unit toward the ___________ rib, which remains fixed to the sternum and the 1st thoracic vertebra.
Intervertebral discs are ___________ in the cervical region and become progressively ___________ toward the lumbar region.
The vertebral artery ascends to the brain by passing through a foramen located in the ___________ process of each ___________ vertebra.
The first two cervical vertebrae, named the ___________ and the ___________, are structurally atypical compared to C3–C6.
The bony peg-like projection arising from the body of the axis, around which the atlas rotates, is called the ___________.
C7 is clinically termed the ___________ because of its long, easily palpable, non-bifid spinous process.
The xiphoid process gives attachment to the ___________ muscle superiorly and, via the linea alba, to the muscles of the ___________ wall inferiorly.
Ribs 8 to 10 are classified as ___________ ribs because their costal cartilages fuse with the cartilage of the rib immediately ___________ them, articulating only indirectly with the sternum.
The supraspinous ligament connects the tips of the spinous processes and extends from the ___________ to the ___________.
Lumbar vertebrae lack costal facets and a foramen transversarium; instead, they are distinguished by their large size and substantial ___________ processes for muscle attachment.
The coccyx articulates superiorly with the ___________ of the sacrum via the ___________ joint.
On each lateral surface of the sacrum, an ___________-shaped surface articulates with the ilium to form the ___________ joint.
Ten of the twelve ribs form a joint between their ___________ and the ___________ process of the lower of the two vertebrae they contact.
The primary thoracic and sacral curvatures are retained through adulthood but become relatively more separated once the secondary ___________ and ___________ curvatures develop after birth.
The anterior sacral foramina and posterior sacral foramina both serve to transmit ___________ nerves, while the auricular surfaces transmit forces to the ___________ joints bilaterally.
